memory_update.text: PDFS is the highest-purity underfollowed candidate for semiconductor manufacturing analytics, secure equipment connectivity, and supply-chain orchestration software.

ONTO and CAMT are adjacent discovery candidates: not pure software, but their inspection/metrology/process-control data layers may become more strategically important as advanced packaging and AI/HPC yield ramps intensify.

TSM should be treated as a reference ecosystem anchor, not an alpha-discovery candidate, for mapping which orchestration, equipment-connectivity, analytics, metrology, and test-data vendors are embedded in advanced manufacturing workflows.

Need follow-up evidence on software revenue mix, recurring revenue, customer concentration, and explicit fab/foundry/OSAT/equipment-vendor adoption for PDFS, ONTO, and CAMT before promoting any candidate beyond Layer 1.

PDFS should remain the primary underfollowed direct candidate for the semiconductor orchestration software node because evidence directly maps Exensio, Cimetrix, secureWISE, and DEX-like collaboration to fab/equipment/OSAT/test data workflows.

ONTO and NVMI are not pure orchestration software vendors, but they are credible adjacent process-control and metrology analytics suppliers where data quality and yield analytics can become capacity-enabling chokepoints.

CAMT belongs in a speculative-shadow lane: advanced packaging inspection and visual AI could feed the manufacturing data layer, but evidence must prove software differentiation or recurring analytics exposure.

Need stronger primary evidence on customer-level adoption: named fabs, OSATs, equipment OEMs, AI/HPC programs, revenue contribution from software/connectivity, and whether these tools are mandatory in high-volume manufacturing rather than optional analytics overlays.

PDFS is the highest-purity underfollowed candidate for the semiconductor orchestration software node because Exensio and secureWISE map directly to manufacturing analytics and secure equipment connectivity.

ONTO, CAMT, and NVMI are not pure software orchestration names, but each may be a second-order data-gate beneficiary because process-control, inspection, and metrology systems generate the data used to improve yield and ramp advanced packaging or advanced-node production.

The investable bottleneck may split into two layers: pure orchestration/connectivity software, where PDFS is most direct, and metrology/inspection-derived process data, where ONTO, CAMT, NVMI, and reference leader KLAC participate.

Layer 2 should verify whether software/data revenue is separately material for ONTO, CAMT, and NVMI; otherwise they may be better classified as equipment beneficiaries rather than orchestration software bottlenecks.

Customer evidence is the critical gap: verify direct use by leading fabs, OSATs, HBM manufacturers, advanced packaging lines, and semiconductor equipment OEMs before promoting any candidate beyond Layer 1.

PDFS should be the primary underfollowed direct candidate for semiconductor orchestration software due to Exensio analytics, secureWISE secure equipment connectivity, Cimetrix/equipment integration, and cross-tier fabless/IDM/foundry/OSAT positioning.

COHU is a plausible second-order small-cap candidate because backend test/inspection equipment data, DI-Core, InSight, and PAICe may connect test-cell automation to yield analytics and factory visibility.

CAMT belongs in the discovery lane as an inspection/metrology data-generation and visual-AI adjacency, especially for advanced packaging, OSAT, and HBM-related flows, but the software/orchestration claim remains a hypothesis.

ONTO is useful as a reference pricing/capability anchor for process-control and analytics software embedded in semiconductor manufacturing equipment, but it is less underfollowed and less pure than PDFS.

Next layer should verify software revenue purity, recurring revenue, customer identity, deployment criticality, and whether these tools are production-orchestration systems rather than auxiliary analytics dashboards.

TSMC is included only as a reference anchor and direct ecosystem/platform owner, not as an underfollowed discovery candidate. Layer 1B expanded the universe around the software/data chokepoint that connects semiconductor manufacturing equipment, fabs, OSATs, test operations, and yield-ramp workflows. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is PDF Solutions, which has explicit semiconductor analytics, equipment-connectivity, secure remote-access, and data-exchange exposure. Onto Innovation and Nova are adjacent but relevant process-control and metrology vendors where software/analytics convert inspection and metrology data into yield and capacity gains. Camtek is a more equipment-heavy speculative-shadow candidate tied to advanced packaging inspection/metrology and visual AI, useful as a second-order data-generation node rather than a pure orchestration platform. This is research-universe expansion only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded the universe around a narrow software/data bottleneck inside semiconductor manufacturing: yield analytics, process-control data, secure tool connectivity, metrology-derived production visibility, and fab/OSAT collaboration.
